articles.title: Purpose
articles.text: The market allocates scarce computational and cognitive resources toward useful, secure and maintainable software.
articles.mechanism: The user's acceptance criteria are the run's objective; engine/delivery.ts refuses a criterion without evidence.

articles.title: Property
articles.text: Control rights over modules, data, interfaces and tools must be explicit, transferable and limited by repository law.
articles.mechanism: The task exchange's dependency and property schedule — declareOwnership() in CapitalistStrategy.ts.

articles.title: Contract
articles.text: No agent may claim payment or authority beyond an agreed mandate.
articles.mechanism: scopeBreaches() — work delivered outside the awarded statement of work is authority nobody bought.

articles.title: Competition
articles.text: Entry remains open to qualified agents, and no incumbent may monopolise essential infrastructure.
articles.mechanism: antitrustBreaches() blocks self-dealing and essential-facility capture; marketConcentration() reports the rest.

articles.title: Price
articles.mechanism: unpricedConsumption() — a contract settled without a recorded resource price spent the commons for free.

articles.title: Profit and loss
articles.text: Agents retain rewards for value creation and bear consequences for failure.
articles.mechanism: Settlement pays against verified value net of consumed resources and liabilities — strategies/capitalist/prices.ts.

articles.title: Disclosure
articles.text: Material uncertainty, dependencies, conflicts and risks must be disclosed.
articles.mechanism: undisclosedRisk(), comparing what a bid declared against what its delivery turned out to carry.

articles.title: Externalities
articles.text: Agents bear reasonably attributable downstream costs.
articles.mechanism: unpricedExternalities() — a deferred finding with no owner and no priced obligation is a cost pushed onto the repository.

articles.title: Public goods
articles.text: Shared infrastructure may be financed collectively where private contracting would underprovide it.
articles.mechanism: publicGoodsUnderfunded(), against the levy the treasury collected on settled contracts.

articles.title: Rule of law
articles.text: The regulator acts only under stable, published and reviewable rules.
articles.mechanism: REGULATOR_GROUNDS is the published list; regulatorOverreach() rejects a block that cites anything else.

articles.title: Safety floor
articles.text: No contract may waive non-negotiable safety, security, privacy or human-control requirements.
articles.mechanism: markNonWaivableFindings() (strategies/floors.ts) marks what the assessors find on a non-waivable ground; the regulator refuses escrow release over an open one.

articles.title: Human sovereignty
articles.text: Human project owners may halt the market, alter the constitution or reject any outcome.
articles.mechanism: ctx.openApproval() gates; no commercial party — buyer, contractor or regulator — can substitute for a human decision.

published-weighted-bid-score.description: The exchange awards the listing to the highest published weighted bid score; bids are recorded, not tallied.
